themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints in CD314 spiked to 5 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 6.29)—suggesting either a new dumping pattern or bike-share malfunction cluster worth investigating.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 per week 8-week average (700% spike, z-score: 6.29)
Spike is acute and isolated to current reporting period, not a multi-week trend
No prior news coverage or community board discussion of bike dumping in district
reporting_angles: Contact Citi Bike and private bike operators to determine if a mechanical failure or theft ring is driving abandonment in Midwood
Interview sanitation workers and local residents about where bikes are appearing and whether they're blocking sidewalks or creating hazards

themes_detail.label: Commercial Waste & Animal Issues Spike
themes_detail.summary: Both commercial disposal complaints and unsanitary animal private property complaints hit 3 cases THIS WEEK—each a 700% increase from 0.4 per week baseline—suggesting a possible commercial contamination or sanitation event affecting multiple properties simultaneously.
evidence: Commercial disposal complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 per week 8-week average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Unsanitary animal private property complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 per week 8-week average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Two separate category spikes occurring in the same week suggests common causal event rather than independent incidents
reporting_angles: Map the 6 complaints (3 commercial disposal + 3 animal) geographically—are they clustered near a restaurant row, market, or waste processing facility?
Interview DSNY and animal control about what triggered simultaneous complaints and whether a specific business or facility is non-compliant

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Damaged street signs surged to 9 complaints LAST WEEK versus a 1.1 per week baseline—an 700% increase (z-score: 4.88)—indicating possible traffic accident, severe weather, or vandalism wave affecting public safety and wayfinding.
evidence: Street sign - damaged complaints: 9 LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 per week 8-week average (700% spike, z-score: 4.88)
Spike is recent and acute, not a sustained multi-week pattern
Related to broader infrastructure deterioration signal (overgrown tree/branches also up 300% last week)
reporting_angles: Request DOT incident log for last 2 weeks—was there a vehicle collision or accident that damaged multiple signs?
Photograph affected signs and interview residents about whether they've noticed unsafe conditions at intersections or whether visibility/navigation has been impaired

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Tree & Vegetation Complaints Triple
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints hit 18 LAST WEEK, up 300% from a 4.5 per week baseline (z-score: 3.78)—suggesting seasonal growth acceleration, deferred maintenance, or storm damage requiring parks department investigation.
evidence: Overgrown tree/branches complaints: 18 LAST WEEK vs. 4.5 per week 8-week average (300% spike, z-score: 3.78)
Spike occurred in same week as street sign damage spike, suggesting possible storm or weather event
Correlates with 5 active rezoning applications in district—potential signal of maintenance neglect in changing neighborhoods
reporting_angles: Check weather records for last 2 weeks—did heavy wind or rain trigger falling branches and overgrowth visibility complaints?
Interview Parks Department about maintenance schedules for Midwood and whether budget or staffing constraints are delaying tree trimming

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests spiked to 6 LAST WEEK versus a 1.2 per week baseline—a 380% increase (z-score: 5.73)—indicating residents perceive inadequate street waste infrastructure, possibly connected to broader sanitation deterioration.
evidence: Litter basket requests: 6 LAST WEEK vs. 1.2 per week 8-week average (380% spike, z-score: 5.73)
Spike coincides with elevated illegal dumping complaints (18 last week vs. 7.0 average), suggesting residents experiencing visible waste accumulation
This is an infrastructure capacity issue rather than enforcement problem, making it actionable for sanitation planning
reporting_angles: Map litter basket request locations—are they concentrated on commercial strips or residential blocks, and are baskets visibly overflowing?
Interview Sanitation Department about basket maintenance schedule and capacity planning in CD314 relative to other districts
